title: U.S. House · Idaho's 1st District
area: Western Idaho, including Boise's western suburbs, Nampa, Caldwell, and the Idaho Panhandle north to the Canadian border.

context.text: Incumbent Russ Fulcher defeated Andy Briner and Joseph Morrison in the May 19, 2026 Republican primary with 78.2% of the vote. Kaylee Peterson defeated Ken Brungardt in the Democratic primary with 87.1% of the vote. Brendan Gomez advanced from the Constitution Party without a primary after it was canceled.
The Cook Political Report rates this district R+22 by partisan voting index.

summary.text: Russ Fulcher is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Idaho's 1st District, serving since January 2019. He previously served ten years in the Idaho Senate, six as Majority Caucus Chair.

background.text: Graduated from Meridian High School and earned a bachelor's and master's degree in business from Boise State University, along with additional certifications in electronic engineering.
Served in the Idaho Senate for 10 years, six of them as Majority Caucus Chair, and on the Idaho Senate State Affairs and Education Committees.
Sponsored Idaho's grocery tax credit legislation while in the Idaho Senate, which his official biography says has returned about $800 million to Idaho families.

priorities.text: His official biography highlights limiting government influence, easing tax and regulatory burdens, and protecting individual rights as recurring priorities from his time in the Idaho Senate through Congress.
Border security and immigration enforcement, citing his 2020 trip to the southern border and testimony to a House Appropriations subcommittee on the need to fund border security.
Reducing the national debt and deficit, calling the current fiscal trajectory unsustainable and a risk to future generations.

positions.summary: Says he is pro-life, that life begins at conception, and that he has voted against every bill that does not uphold the right to life for the unborn.
positions.quote: I am strongly and consistently pro-life — both at the beginning and at the end of life. Life begins at conception, and every unborn child has the inherent right to life. The unborn are the least capable of defending themselves, and in the most desperate need of protection. I have voted against every bill that does not uphold the right to life for the unborn and my first speech on the House floor emphasized my pro-life values and the need to protect the unborn.

record.text: Currently sits on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce and the House Committee on Natural Resources; previously served on the House Committee on Education and the Workforce.
As an Idaho state senator, sponsored the state's grocery tax credit, which his office says has returned roughly $800 million to Idaho households.

candidates.name: Kaylee Peterson

summary.text: Kaylee Peterson is the Democratic nominee for Idaho's 1st Congressional District. She was born in New London, Connecticut, lives in Eagle, Idaho, and has been active in Idaho Democratic Party youth organizing.

background.text: Earned an associate degree from College of Western Idaho in 2023.
Worked as chief of staff of Associated Students of College of Western Idaho and served on the College Council Executive Board.
Served as president of Idaho Young Democrats.

positions.summary: Platform calls for moving to a universal single-payer health system.
positions.quote: Taking health insurance companies completely out of the equation and moving to a universal single-payer system is the best, most transparent, and cheapest way forward for families.

positions.summary: Platform calls for increasing corporate tax rates and removing corporate tax breaks and subsidies.
positions.quote: Increase corporate tax rates, remove corporate tax breaks/subsidies

positions.summary: Platform calls for increasing the federal minimum wage.
positions.quote: Increase the federal minimum wage, benefit packages, overtime protections, and secure worker pensions.

positions.summary: Platform calls for shutting down private for-profit detention facilities and stopping mass deportations.
positions.quote: It’s time to shut down private for-profit detainment facilities, stop cruel mass deportations, and dismantle the current immigration enforcement bureaucracies

positions.summary: Platform criticizes Idaho's post-Dobbs abortion restrictions and calls for lawmakers to defer to women and medical providers.
positions.quote: it is time for lawmakers to step out of the exam room and listen to women, families, maternal-fetal specialists, and healthcare professionals to protect lives

positions.summary: Platform criticizes federal fossil fuel subsidies and rollbacks of clean-energy contracts and calls for expanding solar, wind, nuclear and geothermal energy.
positions.quote: Gutting clean and renewable energy contracts has stripped lucrative job opportunities away from Idaho trades

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website or Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey found; only a brief Ballotpedia biography was available within the research budget for this race.

candidates.name: Brendan Gomez
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Constitution Party without a primary after it was canceled.

summary.text: Brendan Gomez is the Constitution Party candidate for Idaho's 1st Congressional District. He previously ran for Idaho State Senate District 22 in 2022 and for this U.S. House seat in 2024, both as the Constitution Party candidate. According to state court records cited by the Idaho Capital Sun (Sept. 17, 2026), he was charged with 10 counts of willfully possessing child sex abuse material and, under a plea agreement, pleaded guilty to two counts of possession of sexually exploitative materials; sentencing is scheduled for Nov. 16, and the state recommended a fixed term of three years with 12 years indeterminate. The article said his attorney could not be immediately reached.

priorities.text: In his Vote411 answer, says he would initiate a "Mass Treason Investigation" if elected.
priorities.quote: As a member of Congress, I aim to initiate a Mass Treason Investigation that investigates the Republican Party's open collusion with Russia starting in 2016 and the Democrats' failure to expel, impeach, and imprison those who are guilty of violating the Constitution and threatening National Security.

priorities.text: Lists economic collapse, a lack of a living wage, the war on renters, unaffordable healthcare costs, and inadequate education among the challenges he says face the nation.

candidates.researchNotes: Only a Vote411 (League of Women Voters) candidate answer was found; it does not take positions on specific guide issues. He did not respond to the Idaho Capital Sun 2026 questionnaire. No campaign website was found. The criminal case is described in his summary from the Idaho Capital Sun report; court records were not independently accessed.

statements.quote: Economic collapse, religious tyranny, drug abuse, a lack of a living wage, the war on renters, unaffordable healthcare costs, and inadequate education are but a few of the catastrophes plaguing the nation.
statements.context: In his League of Women Voters / Vote411 answer on the most significant challenges facing Idaho and the U.S.

candidates.name: Sarah Zabel

summary.text: Sarah Zabel is an Independent candidate who retired from the U.S. Air Force in 2018 as a major general, later wrote a book on the science of depression, and worked as an adjunct for the RAND Corporation before entering the race in November 2025.

background.text: Retired from the U.S. Air Force in 2018 as a major general.
Wrote a book about the science of depression and worked as an Adjunct for RAND Corporation.

priorities.text: Says the federal government is burdening the economy with tariffs and excessive workforce controls, and that reducing those burdens would make living more affordable.
priorities.quote: The federal government is burdening the economy with tariffs and excessive workforce controls. Reduce those burdens and we can make living more affordable.

priorities.text: Says laws should be reformed and enforced fairly and evenly.
In the Idaho Capital Sun questionnaire, lists her top policy priorities as fixing Social Security, lowering health care costs and expanding access, and reducing the annual deficit.
priorities.quote: Fix Social Security—preserving old age and survivors insurance and disability insurance for current and future beneficiaries; lower health care costs and expand access to more Idahoans; and reduce our annual deficit.

positions.summary: Says federal tariffs are burdening the economy and should be reduced to make living more affordable.
positions.quote: The federal government is burdening the economy with tariffs and excessive workforce controls.

positions.summary: In a questionnaire answer on the SAVE Act, says she does not support it, saying the problem it addresses has already been solved.
positions.quote: I don’t support the SAVE Act. It addresses a problem that has already been solved: the threat of non-citizen voting in federal elections.

positions.summary: Her campaign site says she supports tax reform that asks more from those with the highest earnings.
positions.quote: I support tax reform that asks more from those with the highest earnings — not to punish success, but because the alternative is a debt trajectory that no serious person defends.

positions.summary: Her campaign site says service members should be entered into military conflicts only with congressional authorization.
positions.quote: make sure our service members are entered into military conflicts only with the authorization of Congress and the backing of law.

positions.summary: In a questionnaire answer, supports funding border security and deporting people who commit serious crimes, along with green cards for Dreamers and case-by-case review for other undocumented immigrants.
positions.quote: Finally, we need to deal with the roughly 14 million undocumented immigrants already here: deportation for people who commit serious crimes, green cards for Dreamers, and case-by-case review for other groups.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and statements come from her campaign site's What I Stand For page and the Idaho Capital Sun 2026 voter guide questionnaire (her Ballotpedia survey was checked earlier). Her tariff position is from Ballotpedia; her site also criticizes tariffs.

statements.quote: The federal government can help by removing obstacles that drive up building, outfitting, and insurance costs for new housing, starting with tariffs and a broken worker visa system.
To stabilize insurance markets, I’d restore expanded ACA subsidies and fix the “subsidy cliff.”
statements.context: In the Idaho Capital Sun voter guide questionnaire
